scope: Proposition 3.5 (Diagramwise factorization) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 18-19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Split the labels into S = S1 ⊔ S2 and the roots into R = R1 ⊔ R2, where Ri ⊂ Si. Let γi be a diagram on (Ri, Si). Define ηI(γ1, γ2) to be the indicator that every displayed particle trajectory of γ1 has distance greater than ε throughout I from every displayed trajectory of γ2. This includes detached groups and includes the initial and terminal times. For a single global diagram γ, define ηI(γ; S1, S2) by the same condition between its labelled paths in S1 and S2, using their prescribed force-group flows. On this indicator, merge the two root groups, and take the union of the two batches at each generation, padding a finished list by empty batches. This gives a diagram on (R, S). Conversely, every nonzero diagram term satisfying ηI(γ; S1, S2) = 1 splits uniquely in this manner. Its detached groups necessarily belong to one Si, and its root flow splits over its two intersections with Si. Under 18 this bijection the signed transport measures, with this indicator imposed, agree with the tensor product of the two diagram transport measures: σ(γ)wI(γ)HI R,A ηI = ηI [︁ σ(γ1)wI(γ1)HI R1,A1 ⊗ σ(γ2)wI(γ2)HI R2,A2 ]︁ . (3.12) Summation over the bijection preserves this equality. Factorial weights split as (︄ m1 + m2 m1 )︄ µm1+m2 (m1 + m2)! = µm1 m1! µm2 m2! . (3.13)
